subject: Private deployment: network egress, retention & ownership (follow-up)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Infra <infra@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Private deployment: network egress, retention & ownership (follow-up)

Hi Elena — great conversation earlier, thanks to you and the infra team for taking the time. Quick recap + asks so we can move towards a concrete private/VPC deployment plan.

Summary from today
- Goal: private deployment (customer VPC / on-prem) for PHI-adjacent workloads with tight egress controls and 3rd-party logging.
- Constraints discussed: no permanent open egress to public endpoints, strict retention for PHI, and separation of telemetry from customer data.

Open items we need to qualify (please confirm and add):
1) PII/PHI scope — does the dataset that will route through Redwood include full PHI (diagnoses, notes) or a redacted subset? Any fields we should treat as high-risk (SSN, medical identifiers)?
2) Retention windows — you mentioned 7 years for clinical records. Please confirm retention required for logs/metadata (SIEM, audit trails) vs model inputs/outputs.
3) Logging controls — desired retention period, must-have redaction/obfuscation rules, and whether logs may leave Acme's us-east-1 environment.
4) Network boundary / egress model — confirm whether you can accept outbound to a fixed IP whitelist (Redwood-managed egress IPs) or if traffic must go via a customer-managed proxy (we noted you may prefer proxy/NAT). Also, is VPC peering allowable or strictly disallowed for private deployments?
5) Air-gap/On-prem constraints — any scheduled audits or airgap requirements (e.g., fully offline maintenance windows) that would affect our autoscaling and update paths?
6) Compliance artifacts — SOC2 type II report, encryption-at-rest details, KMS/HSM usage: which artifacts are required for procurement?

Attached: requested_evidence_list.xlsx (starter list) — please fill or mark items you already have in your control plane.

Proposed next steps
- Acme: return the evidence list and confirm items 1-5 above (ideally by EOD Wed).
- Redwood: produce a 1-page egress diagram and a port/FQDN whitelist for your infra team. Priyom will scope retention and logging design options.
- Schedule a 30-min technical run-through with your infra team; proposed slot Thu 11 Aug 10:00 AM ET — does that work?

If convenient, loop in the security/controls lead so we can align on audit timelines.

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Infra <infra@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 18:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private deployment: network egress, retention & ownership (follow-up)

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline below and attaching a network outline.

1) PII/PHI scope: Primary flow will include patient name, MRN, limited SSN (last 4 only in administrative payloads), encounter notes (PHI). Full SSN not included in normal production. Treat encounter notes as high-risk.
2) Retention windows: Clinical records — 7 years (state-mandated). Audit logs/SIEM: 365 days in primary cluster; we keep aggregated logs for 3 years. If Redwood needs longer retention for troubleshooting, that must be negotiated and defined as non-PII derivatives only.
3) Logging controls: All raw request/response payloads with PHI must remain inside our account. We will allow redacted metadata (request size, latency, token counts) to be exported to a monitoring account. SIEM sits in us-east-1.
4) Network boundary / egress model: We cannot accept VPC peering with vendor-managed subnets for security reasons. Outbound from our environment must go through our corporate proxy (NAT) or allowlist to a fixed set of external IPs; we prefer the proxy path. We will provide the proxy FQDNs.
5) Air-gap/on-prem: We run quarterly offline maintenance windows; during those windows any external updates must be paused. We would need a plan for software/patch delivery that supports this cadence.
6) Compliance artifacts: Please provide SOC2 Type II and encryption-at-rest + KMS details. We also need a statement of data residency showing logs remain in us-east-1 unless otherwise agreed.

Attached: acme_network_outline.pdf (high-level diagram).

Requests for Redwood
- One-page egress diagram that shows proxy path and any external IPs we would need to allow.
- List of ports/FQDNs and TLS requirements.
- Short note on how Redwood redacts/stores telemetry vs raw payloads in private deployments.

I've CC'd infra@acmehealth.com — they'll send the proxy FQDNs and the retention policy extract.

Thanks,
Elena Ortiz
Head of Partnerships & Integrations
Acme Health
elena.ortiz@acmehealth.com

--

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Acme Health Infra <infra@acmehealth.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private deployment: network egress, retention & ownership (follow-up)

Elena — really helpful, thank you. Confirming next steps and owners below; I added a couple internal notes so we can prepare the materials requested.

Summary of what Acme confirmed
- PHI in scope: encounter notes + patient identifiers (MRN, name); SSN limited to last-4 in admin flows.
- Retention: clinical records 7 years; SIEM raw logs 365 days, aggregates 3 years; raw payloads with PHI must remain in Acme account.
- Egress: no vendor peering; proxy/NAT preferred — infra to send proxy FQDNs.
- Air-gap: quarterly offline windows — Redwood must support paused updates.

Action items
- Jordan (me): produce 1-page egress diagram (proxy path + minimal external endpoints) and a ports/FQDNs whitelist. Deliverable: PDF + diagram link. Target: Tue 10 Aug EOD.
- Priyom Das: draft two retention/logging configurations (a) conservative: keep telemetry within Acme account + short-term debug extracts; (b) pragmatic: redacted telemetry exported to monitoring account with 90-day retention. Also include sample audit log format. Target: Wed 11 Aug 12:00 PM ET.
- Lauren Bishop: prepare a short procurement checklist (SOC2, DPA clauses, timeline for legal review). Target: Wed 11 Aug EOD.
- Acme Infra: share proxy FQDNs and any required IP allowlist; share the retention policy extract. Target: Tue 10 Aug 5:00 PM ET.

I'll attach the draft egress diagram to the shared Drive folder and post the HubSpot update (deal ACME-2027-PVT-01). If Thu 11 Aug 10:00 AM ET still works for a technical review, I'll send a calendar invite; else propose alternate times.
